Singular values and vectors of an operator

Source: R/svds.R
svds.Rd

Golub-Kahan-Lanczos with full reorthogonalisation, run against the operator's action and its adjoint. The result records what converged, what residual each triplet reached, and what argument establishes the bound on the singular values.

Usage

svds(
  A,
  k,
  which = "largest",
  tol = 1e-10,
  maxit = NULL,
  ncv = NULL,
  v0 = NULL,
  seed = 1L,
  method = "auto",
  floor_const = SOLVE_FLOOR_CONST,
  norm_control = list()
)

Arguments

A

A `linop`. Both the forward action and the adjoint are needed.

k

How many singular triplets.

which

`"largest"` or `"smallest"`. RSpectra's `"LM"` and `"SM"` are accepted for the same two. The algebraic forms are not separate names here because a singular value is non-negative.

tol

Convergence tolerance on the backward error and the relative residual of the augmented eigenpair, each plus the arithmetic floor: the certificate's `backward error` and `residual` rows.

maxit

Total applies of the operator, in either mode, across all restarts.

ncv

Subspace size per restart. Storage is `ncv` vectors of each length. `NULL` takes the engine's default.

v0

Starting vector in the domain, or `NULL` for a seeded random one. `"golub-kahan"` only.

seed

Seed for the starting vector. The caller's random stream is restored afterwards.

method

`"auto"`, `"golub-kahan"` or `"primme"`. `"golub-kahan"` is the reference implementation in this package; `"primme"` is the PRIMME library, available when the `linop.primme` package is installed. `"auto"` takes PRIMME when it is available and Golub-Kahan otherwise, and the certificate's `dispatch` records every engine considered and why. The reported singular values are Rayleigh quotients `Re(u^H A v)` of the returned unit vectors, measured on `A`, whichever engine ran.

floor_const

`c` in the arithmetic floor of the certificate.

norm_control

Arguments for the `||A||` estimate.

Value

An object of class `linop_svd`, with `d`, `u`, `v` and the `certificate`. A run that exhausts its budget returns the best triplets it reached and a `fail` certificate rather than an error, and it may hold fewer than `k` of them: nothing is padded.

Details

The certificate is the certificate of the corresponding eigenpair of the hermitian augmented operator, so `residual`, `backward error` and `forward error` mean there exactly what they mean for [eigs()].

`which = "smallest"` is accepted and is the hard end of the problem: a Krylov space reaches the largest singular values first, so the smallest need a subspace approaching the rank of the operator. The certificate reports what was reached rather than the request being refused.

Examples

A <- linop(rbind(diag(c(3, 2, 1)), 0))
fit <- svds(A, k = 2)
fit$d
